claims.text: High-temperature surface segregation driven by differential elemental diffusion undermines the chemical stability of near-equiatomic, multi-element solid-solution nanoparticles.
High-temperature surface segregation driven by differential elemental diffusion undermines the structural stability of these nanoparticles.
Adding a minor fraction of a high-melting-point refractory element suppresses surface segregation.
Suppressing surface segregation through refractory-element addition enhances high-temperature stability.
The relevant starting materials are nanoparticles containing multiple principal elements in near-equiatomic proportions.
Near-equiatomic, multi-element solid-solution nanoparticles can be synthesized using physical or chemical fabrication methods.
Tungsten is an example of a high-melting-point refractory dopant suitable for addition at 1–5 at%.
The proposed stability effect should occur under both oxidative and inert atmospheres across 473–1923 K.
Under thermal stress, more-mobile alloying elements diffuse toward and segregate at the nanoparticle surface.
Surface segregation compromises the metastable solid-solution state.
A refractory dopant has sufficiently reduced diffusivity to act as a diffusion barrier.
The refractory dopant slows overall atomic diffusion and thereby suppresses surface segregation.
Relative to identically prepared undoped nanoparticles, refractory-doped nanoparticles will develop smaller surface-composition gradients and less phase segregation after high-temperature exposure.
Refractory-doped nanoparticles will retain a more uniform elemental distribution than the undoped baseline.
Refractory-doped nanoparticles will preserve structural integrity better than the undoped baseline during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The magnitude of the dopant effect may depend on dopant concentration, nanoparticle size, and alloy system.
Coarsening and support-interfacial reactions may provide alternative degradation mechanisms.
The doped and undoped samples will be prepared identically apart from refractory-element addition and tested under matching thermal and atmospheric conditions.
